A Sandevistan is a spinal implant that slows the world around you: zombies inside its bubble (about 16 tiles) crawl at a fraction of their speed while you run and strike faster. <LINE> <LINE> ACTIVATE: press the activation key (default Z; change it in Options > Mods > Sandevistan). Press it again to cut the implant off. The floating panel and the Implant tab of the character window show Heat, Neural Load, rejection and adaptation.

Every second the implant is on builds Heat. At 100 it cuts out on its own (a thermal cutout) and stays locked until it cools to 0. A manual shutdown is free and keeps your Heat. <LINE> <LINE> Higher adaptation levels lower the heat rate and cool you faster. Each overdrive collapse lowers your Heat ceiling (a thermal scar) by a few points; it recovers with time and sleep.

Using the implant builds Neural Load. From 60 you get symptoms: screen glitches, nosebleeds, the neural monitor complaining. At 80 cyberpsychosis sets in: whispers, blackouts, fury, terrors at night. Rest and antidepressants lower it. <LINE> <LINE> The only way out of cyberpsychosis: remove the implant and spend 5 days without any. The first 2 days are rough: stress and fatigue creep up. It leaves a neural scar: the next implant loads a bit faster. <LINE> <LINE> In a fury (cyberpsychosis) your melee weapons wear twice as fast. <LINE> <LINE> Adaptation lowers the load each use adds (up to -25%% at stable adaptation). Immunosuppressant coverage lowers it further and doubles how fast it decays.

Your body rejects the implant. Untreated, rejection climbs and at 100 the implant is destroyed (about three days). Immunosuppressants cover you while active: Clinical 48 h, Homemade 24 h (nausea, and it can fail) and Herbal 8 h (it accumulates toxicity). <LINE> <LINE> Each unit holds 3 doses: use them from the inventory menu. <LINE> <LINE> The dose option shows what it will do before you take it (rejection before and after, hours of coverage). Coverage also lowers the neural load each use adds. <LINE> <LINE> THE DOWNSIDE: each dose lowers your defenses (immunodepression, the broken-shield moodle). While coverage lasts it stays above a floor (clinical 50); afterwards it falls on its own in a few hours, slower if you are sick. With low defenses wounds get infected more and heal slower, and colds and spoiled food hit harder: disinfect, bandage cleanly and keep antibiotics at hand. Stacking doses (shock dosing) cuts neural load even more, but each extra dose lasts less and, if you overdid it, a rejection rebound comes when it ends.

The Sandevistan Adaptation skill grows with use and unlocks stronger slowdown, lower Heat and faster cooling. Lab prototypes (P05 and the homemade P06) cap at level 5; military grade goes up to 10 and is the most stable. <LINE> <LINE> Wear makes an implant run hotter: a worn one can be calibrated (Electrical 3 and First Aid 4). <LINE> <LINE> While the implant is on, climbing fences, windows and walls and bump stumbles stop failing with a chance equal to your adaptation; at stable adaptation (level 5 lab, 7 military) they never fail. <LINE> <LINE> Hover over a level square of the skill in the Skills tab to see exactly what that level gives, including how long the Overdrive lasts (lab up to 4 s, military up to 7 s).

Installing needs a scalpel, a suture needle (or a sewing needle and thread), disinfectant and a mirror (or standing in front of one); someone else can operate on you and you can operate on them (they choose whether to accept). Removing it is a longer, riskier surgery. <LINE> <LINE> You can also extract the implant from an ex-subject's body with a scalpel: the more First Aid you have, the less worn it comes out (First Aid 4 or more: perfect). With only a knife it is rougher: extra wear, twice the time and a chance to cut your hand.

The Sandevistan tab of the crafting menu has the synthetic compound, the immunosuppressants, the homemade Black Lace and the five parts (neural board, thermal regulator, power cell, chassis and harness) of Prototype 06. Notebooks and reports teach the recipes; the part quality you craft sets the prototype's wear. <LINE> <LINE> Each part needs a single skill (board and cell: Electrical; regulator: Welding; chassis: none, it takes more materials; harness: Tailoring) and the assembly only First Aid, so on a server everyone can specialize and trade parts. Studying an implant teaches you its design, and with paper and a pen you can write blueprints to teach it to others. The military implant can be replicated too (Mk. II): you need to study a working military unit while carrying both military dossiers complete, and build the parts (a military-grade microchip that can be built with lots of work).

The implant takes up to two software chips: a System one (how it handles Heat, neural load and rejection) and a Skill one (what it lets you do). An empty slot is the usual behavior. To install a chip: right-click it in the inventory (10 seconds, with the implant off). Every change adds 3 rejection and leaves the implant recalibrating for one game hour (Heat rises 10 %% faster). To look at or remove the installed chips: right-click the equipped Sandevistan or the floor, in the Firmware menu; if your implant is explanted, the chips come back to your inventory. <LINE> <LINE> Programs are written: you need a blank chip (built with Electrical 4, or found now and then in electronics shops, laboratories and offices) and a computer with power, or a portable terminal (it cannot be built: you find it in military places) which uses one battery per program. It does not ask for Electrical: it is code. What counts is how used to the implant you are: each program occurs to you when you reach a given adaptation level (the Implant tab tells you how many you know and at which level the next one comes) and writing it takes less the more adapted you are (60 down to 25 seconds). Military designs (the Cryo Chamber) also ask for a military microchip. <LINE> <LINE> A chip that comes already programmed (very rare: laboratories, army depots and the military base) can be installed right away or decompiled on a computer with power or with the terminal: you learn the program even if your level is short of it, and the chip is left blank. Carrying both complete military dossiers also teaches Cryo Chamber.
